FINDING_ID: IM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.95  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82  
DESCRIPTION: `process_round()` feeds `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_model_round()` with an incorrect failure signal: `failed = mid not in responses or not responses[mid].parseable`. This treats only missing/unparseable responses as failures and ignores actual immune-relevant failures already detected by `FailureHandler` such as `TIMEOUT`, `EMPTY`, `FORMAT`, and `UNDERPERFORM`. As a result, the immune layer undercounts consecutive model failures, misses `model_failure_*` diagnoses, and can fail to trigger the `model_failure` remediation chain (`add_to_pre_decompose`) for the very cases it is supposed to correct. This is a direct integration bug between the failure subsystem and immune subsystem.  
PROPOSED_FIX: In `process_round()`, derive `failed` from the actual failure detection result already computed earlier, e.g. `failed = failures.get(mid) is not None`, or more narrowly from the subset of failure types intended to count as “model failure” for immune purposes. Pass response time and response char count from `responses[mid]` at the same point so the monitor has coherent per-model round data.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.92  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86  
DESCRIPTION: `_apply_transform("add_synthesis_directive")` only injects the directive for models that do **not** already have a per-model directive: `if model.model_id not in self.config.per_model_directives`. This means the remediation silently skips any model that already has a registry-loaded directive, even though those models may be precisely the ones participating in the pathology. Because per-model directives are preloaded from registry policy, this remediation will often have partial or zero effect while still being recorded as an applied adaptation. That breaks the semantics of the remediation chain and can produce false “applied but ineffective” outcomes unrelated to the actual intervention.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Merge directives instead of skipping existing ones. Append or compose the synthesis directive onto the existing directive text with delimiter/newline handling, bounded by `max_per_model_directive_chars`. If the combined text would exceed the limit, either truncate deterministically with logging or treat the step as unapplied and return `None`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: `record_model_round()` supports parser-yield and cost-per-finding diagnostics using `response_time` and `response_chars`, but `process_round()` never passes those values; it calls `record_model_round(mid, fc, failed)` and relies on defaults `response_time=0.0` and `response_chars=0`. This makes the parser-yield anomaly detector (`response_chars > 2000 and finding_count == 0`) and CPF spike detector (`response_time / findings > 2σ`) effectively dead in normal operation. The immune layer advertises these diagnoses but the integration does not supply the required data.  
PROPOSED_FIX: In `process_round()`, fetch `resp = responses.get(mid)` and call `record_model_round(mid, fc, failed, response_time=resp.response_time if resp else 0.0, response_chars=len(resp.content) if resp else 0)`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor.false_positive_rate` claims to compute a rate over the “last 10 rounds”, but `total_detections` is counted over **all** diagnoses ever emitted, while `natural_resolutions` is windowed by round. This denominator/numerator mismatch biases the rate downward over time, making the Level-3 self-diagnosis increasingly unable to detect a genuinely high recent false-positive rate. The bug affects self-adjustment of immune sensitivity and can suppress needed recalibration.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Window both numerator and denominator consistently. Store detection round on each diagnosis or in a parallel log, then compute `total_detections` only for the same recent window used for natural resolutions.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` judges improvement for `target == "vocab_growth"` using the generic rule `current_val > old_val`, but the `vocab_saturation` remediation lowers `tau_vocab_growth`, not the observed vocab growth metric itself. A successful remediation may leave `vocab_growth` unchanged or still low while correctly preventing premature stop behavior through threshold change. The verification target is therefore mismatched to the mechanism of the fix, causing false “INEFFECTIVE” escalation for a conceptually correct adjustment.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Verify against the actual pathology predicate or downstream decision, not the raw metric. For `vocab_saturation`, compare whether false-positive saturation diagnoses cease, whether `vocab_saturated()` no longer fires prematurely, or store/verify the thresholded condition directly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: `apply_diagnosis()` applies detector damping by `diagnosis.detector`, not by adjusted parameter or chain. This blocks distinct diagnoses from the same detector even when they map to different remediations, and fails to block repeated adjustments from different detectors to the same parameter. Example: repeated `verification` diagnoses for different models or repeated `kappa` diagnoses after chain escalation can be suppressed/coalesced incorrectly because the cooldown key is too coarse. The interface summary explicitly frames damping as “minimum rounds between adjustments to the same parameter”; the implementation does not honor that contract.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Enforce damping by parameter name (and optionally scope, e.g. model_id for per-model directives) after resolving the remediation step, not by detector string. Store recent adjustments keyed by `(parameter, scope)` rather than detector.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: The remediation chain coverage is incomplete relative to diagnoses the immune layer actively emits. `DetectorHealthMonitor` can emit `parser_yield`, `monotonic_decline`, `cpf_spike`, `self_diagnosis`, and some `mu` diagnoses, but `apply_diagnosis()` has no remediation path for them and silently returns `None`. This leaves substantial portions of the advertised immune behaviour observational-only despite the subsystem being described as autonomous/self-healing. That is a completeness gap inside the immune response layer.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either add explicit remediation chains/handlers for each emitted pathology class or downgrade those diagnoses in documentation/comments to advisory-only. At minimum, emit an explicit “no remediation available” event when a diagnosis is unhandled so the failure is visible.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.75  
DESCRIPTION: `apply_diagnosis()` records the metric for remediation verification **after** applying the transform: `_apply_transform(...)` then `current_metric = self._get_current_metric(...)` then `set_remediation_state(metric_at_apply=current_metric, ...)`. Because the monitored histories are round-based and unchanged by config mutation within the same round, this usually equals the pre-fix value by accident. But semantically it is wrong and brittle: if a future transform mutates the monitored state directly, the baseline would be contaminated and outcome verification would compare against a post-fix rather than pre-fix metric.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Capture `metric_before = self._get_current_metric(step["target_metric"])` before `_apply_transform()` and pass that stored value to `set_remediation_state()`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `effective_window()` comments say “resolved pathology means we should be LESS sensitive (wider window)” and mention decay-based adaptation, but the implementation ignores `_sensitivity_decay` entirely and only does `base_window + resolved * _sensitivity_growth`. The comments describe a two-sided adaptive mechanism; the code implements only one additive widening rule. This mismatch matters because Level-3 self-diagnosis adjusts `_sensitivity_decay`, yet that parameter currently has no effect on Level-2 diagnosis windows.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either implement the documented decay-based window adaptation using `_sensitivity_decay`, or remove/replace the misleading formal commentary and self-adjustment of `_sensitivity_decay` if additive widening is the intended design.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: `check_dispatch_health()` can repeatedly diagnose verification miscalibration every round once a model is >2σ below population mean, but `apply_diagnosis()` only applies a directive if the model has no existing directive. After the first directive insertion, subsequent diagnoses become inert with no escalation path and no explicit suppression. This creates a noisy repeated-diagnosis/no-op loop in the immune layer.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add deduplication or escalation state for verification diagnoses, and allow directive merging/updating rather than one-shot insertion-only behaviour. Alternatively suppress repeated emissions while the same remediation is active.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

Definitive stance: the immune layer has one major integration defect (failure signal propagation), two dead-path detectors due to missing data plumbing, and several remediation/verification logic errors that materially weaken autonomous self-healing. The priority fixes are IM_F001–IM_F003 first, then IM_F004–IM_F006.
